title: The Rogue Monster
text: “Wow… what a wonderful race, indeed.”
Yuki-chan watched the Filolial race with her eyes absolutely sparkling.
“Would Yuki-chan like to enter as well?”
“Yuki wants to!”
No matter which loop it was, Yuki-chan always loved racing, I say.
“However—”
Yuki-chan clenched her fist. Oh? Was there some reason she didn’t want to enter after all?
“Right now, Yuki must focus on unifying and guiding the flock as its leader. That should wait until the flock’s sense of unity has been strengthened a bit more.”

Yuki-chan was working hard as their leader, indeed. Certainly, everyone was still rather free-spirited, and there wasn’t much of a sense of unity yet. During Elephant’s singing lessons, everyone sang together happily enough, but from Yuki-chan’s perspective, it clearly wasn’t going smoothly. Bit by bit, though, the Filolials were starting to listen to Yuki-chan’s instructions. Though she’d been raised somewhat later than the others, Yuki-chan had grown splendidly into her role as leader.
“Do your best, I say!”
“Of course, Yuki will!”
And so, Yuki-chan and I spent some time wandering around Zeltoble.
“Is this… a place like the one where Motoyasu-sama and Wolf had their match?”
Yuki-chan asked, pointing at the arena from a distance.
“That was a performance, so it’s a bit different, indeed. Though, according to Father, he’s apparently considering making slaves fight each other as part of the show as well.”

Father was reportedly thinking of adding combat performances to the circus lineup because the whip-cracking show had turned out to be surprisingly harsh on everyone involved. In other words, he didn’t want to leave it up to Lazy Pig! When he asked the mixed-breed lizardman and the rabbit man if they wanted to learn how to fight, both answered yes, so he was apparently considering a performance where all three slaves would each have their own matches. It seemed the idea struck him while training with Elephant. The problem, according to Lazy Pig, was that if the fights looked too impressive, it would draw the Three Heroes Church’s attention—so they’d need to keep things somewhat restrained and clumsy-looking to avoid appearing too polished. Quite a troublesome business, I say.
“Hm… there are an awful lot of dull matches going on.”

This time of year, Zeltoble looked lively enough, but apparently the arena itself was rather sluggish. After all, neither Panda, nor Elephant, nor Older Sister were around. It was the season without any of the popular fighters, so to speak. That was probably why the cheering from the arena wasn’t carrying very far.

…Now that I thought about it, it had been a few days since the Waves struck, which meant Takt would be coming to wreck the Coliseum again around now. How should I go about tormenting him this time? Making him choke on humiliation again and again, right there in front of the public in the arena, sounded rather amusing. Killing him outright in the underground Coliseum, where lives were wagered without question, wouldn’t be nearly as fun. I could preemptively stop him from murdering the slave trader and toss him in the pig pen… no, better yet, capture him alive, strand him on Nanase Island together with the other pigs where he can’t leave, and slowly torment him bit by bit.

…Hmm. Making him suffer thoroughly before killing him was already decided, but it was also true that he’d be quite useful as a resource for recovering the Seven Star Weapons. So, following Father’s teachings—thieves are like resources—it was probably best to let Takt swim free for a while as a resource too. At the very least, I should let him swim until around the time of the Spirit Tortoise, tormenting him just enough along the way. Something like “Nanase Island Demon Lord Legend Murder Case ~A New Murder~” had a nice ring to it, perhaps. The problem was how to hold back the storm. Last time, Rival had handled it, but I clearly wasn’t suited for that role.

Hm… since I wanted to run various experiments anyway, even if I couldn’t lock him away, capturing just Takt alone and using him for human experimentation sounded like a fine plan. An eye for an eye, I say. I’d run all sorts of experiments on Takt. After all, I’d finally become capable of human modification myself! I’d make him taste the same suffering the modified Filolial-samas had endured. Regardless of the details, tormenting an overconfident Takt in the Coliseum was clearly a splendid idea.
“Motoyasu-sama, what is this building here?”
Yuki-chan pointed at Zeltoble’s Adventurer’s Guild this time.
“That’s the Guild, indeed. It’s a facility where you can earn money by completing various odd jobs.”
“I see. So one could earn money here instead of through the circus?”
“Indeed, you could. But since we’ve decided to earn our money cheerfully through the circus, we won’t be using it much.”
“I understand.”
And so, Yuki-chan and I went about browsing inside the Adventurer’s Guild.
“Hey… apparently there’s some powerful rogue monster on the loose.”
“Yeah, I heard that too. Gotta check if there’s a bounty on it before deciding whether it’s worth hunting.”

Such idle chatter drifted into my ears. A rogue monster, was it? That sort of thing happened from time to time. With a bounty attached, it’d be quite the lucrative job for anyone confident in their skills. Come to think of it, Itsuki once mentioned that Father might have some quality that attracted monsters to him… Could there be a chance Father and the others might run into one? Surely not… surely they’d be fine.
“Oh yeah, speaking of which, I heard there’s sometimes weirdly out-of-place rogue monsters showing up around Melromarc. What’s that about?”
“Ah, that’s because there’s a noble in that country who keeps monsters on a whim. Word is they’re often smuggled through Zeltoble’s back routes—pretty famous story, that.”
Hm… I felt like I might have seen something like that myself, back when I still hadn’t quite shaken off my game-brain habits.
“Not too long ago, they had someone haul in a two-headed dog. Where was that monster’s habitat again?”
“I saw a Nue—the one that lives out east—getting hauled off to Melromarc too. That noble sure does love monsters.”
“Ages back, there was a story about some merchant who sold that same noble a Cream Alligator egg at a ridiculous price and made a killing.”
…Was there such a monster?
“Word is, if you catch some weird monster, best thing to do is sell it to that noble. Well, whatever happens to it afterward, it’s money in your pocket either way.”

Presumably it was all properly managed. Or perhaps properly disposed of, one way or another? Hm… Father didn’t seem to have any interest in raising and selling slaves, so perhaps proposing a trade in monsters might not be such a bad idea. Buy monsters from around Siltvelt or Shieldfreeden, raise them, and sell them to that particular noble. Not bad at all. Selling off Filolial-sama, though? Absolutely never. Mm… ghk… Filo-tan flashed through my mind. I recalled that in that one loop, Father had apparently made money through monster trading… so perhaps it was best I abandon the idea after all.
“Motoyasu-sama, does this town not have a circus? I think it would be good to search for one, for reference on our performances.”
“Indeed it would. Once we find one, we shall propose it to Father.”

And so, once Yuki-chan and I finished our stroll and investigation around Zeltoble, we headed to the meeting point to wait for Father—only for him to show up looking utterly worn out. Behind him trailed the slaves, battered and bruised, wearing expressions of accomplishment. They all had a look about them as if some deep bond had formed, exchanging friendly fist-bumps with one another.
“Welcome back, Father, indeed. Did something happen?”
“Well… I suppose you could say something happened, yeah.”

And so Father recounted the whole affair. Apparently, he’d been using the slaves to practice formations. The usual routine—Father handling whatever monster appeared while the slaves went on the attack. Since they fought in this formation as a rule, even Big Sister, who’d had so little combat experience, had managed to fight without injury—a splendid method indeed. With the slaves’ levels equalized, they’d apparently been able to fight without any trouble. Wolf, along with the mixed-breed lizardman and rabbit man, had each taken their turns attacking. Though, since Wolf tended to charge in a bit recklessly, it couldn’t be helped that she’d taken some hits along the way.

The problem arose partway through the fighting, Father said. Apparently, an absurdly powerful monster had shown up out of nowhere. Even with Father holding it back, the monster was massive enough that the slaves kept getting knocked flying by its counterattacks, and on top of that, their attacks simply weren’t doing enough damage.
“Everyone! I’ll hold it here, so go call for help! Head to Zeltoble and find Motoyasu-kun or Yuki-chan!”
“B-but…”
“We can’t just—”
“Vwooooooof! Yip—!?”

At that point, apparently, Wolf ignored Father’s orders entirely and leapt straight at the monster, only to get sent flying by its counterattack. The mixed-breed lizardman and the rabbit man exchanged a glance…
“Woooooaaaaaaaaah!”
“Haaaaaaaaah!”
—and rather than fleeing, they too, just like Wolf, apparently charged straight at the monster.
